title: Declining an Offer and Saying Yes

vocabulary.meaning_en: (formal) to politely say no to an offer or invitation
vocabulary.example: I'm afraid I will have to decline your invitation.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a generous offer from someone
vocabulary.example: Thank you for your kind offer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: I agree; we have an agreement
vocabulary.example: Ten percent off? It's a deal!

vocabulary.meaning_en: the answer someone gives in a wedding ceremony to say yes
vocabulary.example: When asked the question, he said, 'I do.'

vocabulary.meaning_en: a formal event with fixed traditions
vocabulary.example: The award ceremony starts at seven.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the ceremony when two people get married
vocabulary.example: My cousin's wedding is next month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you work with
vocabulary.example: All my colleagues came to the party.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you know through work, but not well
vocabulary.example: I met a business acquaintance at the conference.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the place where an event happens
vocabulary.example: The office was the venue for the ceremony.

vocabulary.meaning_en: with very little time to prepare
vocabulary.example: It was all we could get at short notice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: perfect for a purpose
vocabulary.example: This room is ideal for meetings.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to be going to do something very soon
vocabulary.example: The ceremony is about to begin.

vocabulary.meaning_en: please sit down (formal)
vocabulary.example: Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to end someone's job
vocabulary.example: The company fired him for stealing.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to be in charge of an office, team or business
vocabulary.example: She manages the Paris office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a gift given to people who are getting married
vocabulary.example: We bought them a lamp as a wedding present.

vocabulary.meaning_en: words you say when someone has done something good or has good news
vocabulary.example: Congratulations on your new job!

vocabulary.meaning_en: a good end to a story
vocabulary.example: The story has a happy ending.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make someone want to do something good
vocabulary.example: Her success inspired me to study harder.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a formal written agreement
vocabulary.example: He signed the best contract of his career.

fine_lines.title: decline vs refuse vs reject
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الثلاثة تعني «يقول لا». decline أكثرها تهذيبًا ورسمية (للعروض والدعوات). refuse أقوى ومباشرة. reject قوية جدًّا وتعني عدم قبول شيء أو شخص بعد النظر فيه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: All three mean say no. Decline is the most polite and formal (for offers and invitations). Refuse is stronger and direct. Reject is very strong: you don't accept something after looking at it.

examples.sentence: Thank you for your kind offer, but I will have to decline.
He refused to sign the contract.

fine_lines.title: colleague vs acquaintance
fine_lines.explanation_ar: colleague شخص تعمل معه في المكان نفسه. acquaintance شخص تعرفه معرفة سطحية، وbusiness acquaintance شخص تعرفه من خلال العمل لكنه ليس زميلًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A colleague works with you. An acquaintance is someone you know, but not well; a business acquaintance is someone you know through work.

examples.sentence: My colleague sits next to me.
He's a business acquaintance from another company.

expressions.phrase: Thank you for your kind offer, but I will have to decline.
expressions.meaning_ar: شكرًا على عرضك الكريم، لكنني مضطر إلى الاعتذار عن قبوله.
expressions.meaning_en: A very polite way to say no to an offer.
expressions.example: Thank you for your kind offer of a job in Paris, but I will have to decline.
You do the slides and I'll do the report? It's a deal.

expressions.meaning_en: The answer to the question in a wedding ceremony.
expressions.example: The registrar asked the question, and she answered, 'I do!'

expressions.phrase: Please could you take your seats? The ceremony is about to begin.
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تتفضلون بالجلوس من فضلكم؟ الحفل على وشك أن يبدأ.
expressions.meaning_en: A formal request to sit down because an event is starting.
expressions.example: Please could you take your seats? The awards ceremony is about to begin.

expressions.meaning_en: I'm happy to see you; I didn't expect you.
expressions.example: Mr Ahmed! This is a nice surprise. Please come in.

expressions.phrase: It's all we could get at short notice.
expressions.meaning_ar: هذا كل ما استطعنا الحصول عليه في هذا الوقت القصير.
expressions.meaning_en: We had little time, so this was the only choice.
expressions.example: Sorry the room is small - it's all we could get at short notice.

expressions.phrase: Thanks to everyone for making this a special day.
expressions.meaning_ar: شكرًا للجميع على جعل هذا اليوم مميزًا.
expressions.meaning_en: Thanking guests at the end of an event.
expressions.example: Thanks to everyone for making this a special day for our company.

grammar.title: be about to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم am/is/are about to + الفعل في المصدر لشيء سيحدث بعد قليل جدًّا: The ceremony is about to begin (الحفل على وشك أن يبدأ).
grammar.explanation_en: Use am/is/are about to + base verb for something that will happen very soon: The ceremony is about to begin.
examples: The meeting is about to start.
I'm about to leave the office.
We were about to call you.

grammar.title: Polite refusal: Thank you for…, but I will have to / I'm afraid I…
grammar.explanation_ar: لنرفض عرضًا بأدب نبدأ بالشكر ثم نستخدم but مع I will have to decline أو I'm afraid I can't، ويمكن ذكر السبب باختصار.
grammar.explanation_en: To say no politely: thank the person first, then use 'but' + 'I will have to decline' or 'I'm afraid I can't', and give a short reason.
examples: Thank you for your kind offer, but I will have to decline.
Thank you for inviting me, but I'm afraid I can't come.
It's very kind of you, but I'm happy in my current job.

grammar.title: Short answers: Do you…? – I do.
grammar.explanation_ar: في الإنجليزية نجيب عن سؤال يبدأ بـ Do you…? بإجابة قصيرة تكرّر الفعل المساعد: Yes, I do / No, I don't، ولا نكرّر الفعل الرئيسي. ومن ذلك عبارة الزفاف الشهيرة I do.
grammar.explanation_en: We answer 'Do you...?' questions with a short answer using the helper verb: Yes, I do / No, I don't. The famous wedding answer 'I do' is this kind of short answer.
examples: Do you agree? – Yes, I do.
Do you need help? – No, I don't, thanks.
Does she work here? – Yes, she does.

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to say no to an offer?
choices: Thank you for your kind offer, but I will have to decline.
questions.explanation_ar: decline مع الشكر أكثر الطرق تهذيبًا.
questions.explanation_en: Thanking and using 'decline' is the most polite.

questions.question: What does Mr Socrates offer Tom?
choices: a job as manager of the Paris office
questions.explanation_ar: عرض عليه إدارة مكتبه الجديد في باريس.
questions.explanation_en: He offers Tom a job managing the Paris office.

questions.question: A person you work with every day is a…
'Please take your seats' means…
questions.explanation_ar: take your seats أي تفضلوا بالجلوس.

questions.question: Do you need help? – Yes, I ___.
questions.explanation_ar: الإجابة القصيرة تكرر الفعل المساعد do.

questions.question: Tom thanks Mr Socrates but says no. Which word means 'politely say no'?
'It's all we could get at short notice' means…
choices: we had little time, so this was the only choice
questions.explanation_ar: at short notice تعني في وقت قصير.
questions.explanation_en: At short notice = with little time.

questions.question: Which word means 'to end someone's job'?
questions.explanation_ar: fire تعني فصل شخص من العمل.
